html:
The Oseberg ship is a Viking ship buried in a great mound near Tønsberg in 834, with two women and a wealth of goods. It was dug up in 1904.

The ship, about 21 metres long and built of oak, has a richly carved prow. Clay kept the wood and textiles well. In the grave were a carved cart, sledges, beds, tapestries, kitchen gear and the bones of horses and dogs. The carving style gives its name to a phase of Viking art.

Who the women were is unknown; one may have been a queen. With the Gokstad ship, Oseberg showed how the Vikings built the ships that carried them to England, Iceland and beyond. It was shown at the Viking Ship Museum in Oslo, now closed for rebuilding. See Norway.
